reason: The cited evidence supports that ML can predict yield stress and plastic strain in BCC HEAs (E1, E2) and elastic constants in RCCAs (E4), but none of the evidence addresses hierarchical microstructural descriptors, fracture behavior, tensile (vs. compressive) properties, or the specific HfNbTiVAl10 alloy. The claimed 25% error reduction over FEM and the sufficiency of the training data are unsupported assertions.
premises: ML models can predict mechanical properties of HEAs with low error
Hierarchical microstructural descriptors can be quantitatively captured and used as ML features
ML predictions will be faster than FEM simulations
ML predictions will reduce error margins by ~25% compared to FEM for HfNbTiVAl10
Training data from analogous HEA/MEA systems is sufficient to generalize to HfNbTiVAl10
